desc:
You are given an array nums of distinct positive integers and a positive integer target. Count the sequences of numbers, each chosen from nums with repetition allowed, whose sum equals target. The order matters: [1, 2] and [2, 1] are different sequences.

The count can be huge, so return it modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Think about the last number of a valid sequence. What is the sum of everything before it?
If the last number is x, the earlier part is any ordered sequence that sums to target - x. So ways[t] is the sum of ways[t - x] over all x in nums with x ≤ t.
Set ways[0] = 1 (the empty sequence) and fill t = 1..target in increasing order, taking everything modulo 1,000,000,007.
editorial: Let ways[t] be the number of ordered sequences summing to t. Group the sequences by their last element x: removing it leaves an ordered sequence summing to t - x, and every such sequence extended by x is valid. Hence ways[t] = sum of ways[t - x] over all x ≤ t in nums, with ways[0] = 1.

The loop order is what makes the count ordered: the target is the outer loop and the numbers are the inner loop, so every position of a sequence can use every number. Swapping the loops (numbers outside) would count combinations instead, ignoring order. Time O(n · target), space O(target).
